{align=center} **The BB Health Spa (BB)**

Bethany owns The BB Health Spa in Main City in country X. Economic growth has been high for the last few years. The government of country X wants this growth to continue so it has reduced income tax. However, it is also worried about inflation becoming a problem so it has increased interest rates.

The BB Health Spa is very busy and Bethany is considering taking on a partner to help manage the business and give her more free time. However, she has been a sole trader for 10 years and wants the business to stay small.

The customers of The BB Health Spa are people of all ages who are interested in their health. Bethany employs two qualified workers to provide the treatments for customers. Bethany herself also provides customers with treatments. In addition, she does all the administration such as ordering inventory, accounts and paying invoices when the spa is closed.

The BB Health Spa still uses the original treatment equipment which was purchased when the business started. Some spas nearby have the latest equipment but these spas charge much higher prices than The BB Health Spa. Bethany records all the financial transactions by filling in accounts books by hand. This takes her a long time. Customers book appointments using the telephone and Bethany later telephones them to remind them when an appointment is due.

{align=center} **Appendix 1**

{align=center} **Advert for treatments at The BB Health Spa**

{align=center} 

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Weekly forecasts for two possible additional services**

|   | Steam room | Hair cuts |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Additional customers | 200 | 50 |
|   |   |   |
| Average price charged per customer | \$5 | \$25 |
| Wages | \$60 | \$400 |
| Cost of sales | \$40 | \$125 |
| Lease of equipment | \$400 | \$175 |

{align=center} 

{align=center} **Appendix 3**

**Daily News **

{align=right} **September**

{align=center} **New equipment now available in many health spas to make skin look younger**

There have been a number of changes in technology for health spas which allow the treatments to be much more effective in making skin look younger. Many people are keen to try these treatments using the latest equipment to get younger looking skin. This equipment is very expensive for health spas to buy or lease.

The news of these treatments has appeared on social media sites and on mobile phone Apps leading to higher demand. ‘Some customers will pay high prices for such treatments’, said a local health spa owner who is keen to promote his health spa as being one of the first to use the new equipment.

There have also been developments in software which make customer bookings and accounts much easier, quicker and with fewer mistakes. Automatic text (sms) messages are used to remind customers of their appointments – so no need to miss an appointment again.

Look out for these changes in health spas near you!

Explain why the following **three **factors are important to Bethany when choosing a business partner:

- Knowledge of new technology
- Experience in managing a health spa
- Capital to invest.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-01-specimen-2020-paper-2-insert-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Knowledge of new technology is crucial because the spa is still using old equipment while competitors have upgraded **[Ap]**. A partner with technology knowledge could help modernise the spa's equipment and systems, such as implementing software to ease customer bookings and accounting, which Bethany currently does manually **[Ap]**, taking her a long time when she could be focusing on improving other aspects of the business  **[An]**

Experience in managing a health spa is important as it would complement Bethany's skills. Bethany currently does all the administration herself **[Ap]** when the spa is closed. An experienced partner could take on some management responsibilities, giving Bethany more of the free time as she desires **[An]**. Their industry experience could also help BB Health Spa compete against nearby spas that charge much higher prices **[Ap]**

Capital to invest is vital because new technology and equipment for health spas are very expensive **[Ap]**. BB Health Spa likely needs significant funds to upgrade its outdated equipment and implement new booking and accounting systems **[Ap]**. A partner bringing capital could allow these improvements without Bethany having to take on debt **[An]**

While all three factors are important, and the ideal partner would possess all of these characteristics,  knowledge of new technology is likely the most crucial **[E] **for BB Health Spa's future success in the changing industry **[Ap]**. It is already lagging behind competitors **[Ap]** in this respect and, if it is going to remain competitive, the business must become more efficient. Technology is a key way to do this **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Knowledge of new technology**
> 
>   - Operates the latest treatment machines → less staff training → lower costs
>   - Can train other employees → new treatments introduced faster → spa gains an edge over rivals
>   - Possible drawback: partner might feel “more important” than Bethany → tension over who is in charge
> - **Experience in managing a health spa**
> 
>   - Knows day-to-day operations → runs the spa more efficiently → wastes less time and money
>   - Can take over tasks like ordering stock → frees Bethany’s time, which is her main reason for a partnership
>   - Risk of clashes if the partner’s style differs → arguments could hurt efficiency
> - **Capital to invest**
> 
>   - Brings cash for the latest equipment → no bank loan needed → saves interest costs
>   - Extra funds make it easier to expand and match bigger spas with modern treatments
>   - Drawback: partner will want a share of profit and a voice in decisions, reducing Bethany’s control
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Experience in managing a spa would give Bethany the free time she wants, but she might still need to borrow money for new equipment
>   - Knowledge of new technology boosts competitiveness and speeds up training, yet it does not add capital and could leave Bethany doing most management tasks herself
>   - Capital investment removes loan costs and funds expansion, but it will not lighten Bethany’s workload and means sharing control and profits

**Extract:**

{align=center} **Everyone Theatre (ET) **

Zane and Zaara are both actors. They plan to start up a theatre in a low-income area of Main City. Zane and Zaara believe that helping the community is as important as being successful entrepreneurs. 

The theatre will be a private sector business and Zane and Zaara have to decide whether to start up as an unincorporated business (partnership) or as a limited company. Zane is planning to prepare a cash-flow forecast for the first year. Zaara knows they will need to set business objectives for the theatre and also decide on a leadership style to use when managing employees. ET will have 24 part-time employees as shown in the organisational chart in Appendix 1. 

Zane and Zaara plan to put on performances in the evenings for local people and tourists. There will be 100 seats in the theatre but not all the seats will be sold if the price is too high. The Marketing Manager, Zaara, will need to decide which performances to put on, what price to charge and which refreshments to sell. Zaara will also need to decide between the two possible options for the first performance when the theatre opens. Information on the two options is shown in Appendix 2.

In the daytime the theatre building will be used by Daycare, a local social enterprise. Daycare takes care of young children up to the age of 5 so that low-income family members can go out to work. It also provides education for the children which helps their development and progress before they start school. Some of Daycare’s objectives are different to those of ET

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Proposed organisational chart for the theatre**

Note: The numbers in brackets are the number of part-time employees who work in each department

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Forecast data for the two possible options for ET’s first performance at the theatre**

| For each performance | **Option 1** | **Option 2** |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Number of actors/employees | 7 | 24 |
| Average wage cost per actor/employee | \$30 | \$10 |
| All other costs including scenery, costumes and promotion | \$1000 | \$2000 |
| Forecast revenue assuming all 100 seats are sold | \$1000 | \$2500 |

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Email from Zane to Zaara**

**To: Zaara **

**From: Zane **

**Date: 1 April 2023**

We want to support the local community and we need to make decisions about the following. 

Should we: 

- Pay fair wages even though they may be higher than those paid by competing theatres?
- Only buy costumes produced in the local community?
- Purchase all refreshments from suppliers that do not pollute the environment?

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of starting up ET as either an unincorporated business or as a limited company. Which should Zane and Zaara choose? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2023-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
As a partnership, ET would be easy and cheap to set up. Zane and Zaara could make quick decisions about shows and ticket prices **[Ap]**. They would keep all the profits to split between them, which would be their reward for their hard work in setting up the business **[An]**. However, they would have unlimited liability. This means if ET couldn't pay its bills, Zane and Zaara might have to sell their own assets to cover them **[An]**

In contrast, as shareholders of a limited company, Zane and Zaara would have limited liability protection. If ET went bankrupt, they would only lose the money they put in, not their personal savings or homes **[An]**. Being a company might also make it easier to get loans or investors to help with the costs of starting the theatre **[An] **and purchasing props and costumes **[Ap]**. However, setting up a company costs more money and takes more time, and they may need expensive legal and financial advice **[An]**

While a partnership would be simpler, the financial risks are too high for Zane and Zaara **[E]**. The benefits of limited liability and easier fundraising make a company the better choice for ET **[E]** . Starting a theatre in a low-income area of Main City **[Ap] **is risky. They shouldn't put their personal belongings in danger if things go wrong. As a company, ET might find it easier to get money to buy costumes and equipment **[Ap]**. It could also look more professional to customers and to Daycare, the social enterprise they want to work with **[Ap]. **All of these benefits make a private limited company a better choice **[E]**

> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Unincorporated business**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Partners keep full control of the theatre → quick, independent decisions
>     - No shareholders to pay → profits shared only between the two owners → higher income per partner
>     - Easy and cheap to set up the theatre → few legal rules → lower start-up effort and cost
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Unlimited liability → personal assets (house, savings) at risk if debts cannot be paid
>     - Limited capital → only the two partners’ own money to invest → may restrict growth
>     - Each partner is liable for the other’s mistakes → wrong decisions could cause personal financial loss
> - **Private limited company**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Limited liability → owners’ personal possessions are protected if the theatre owes money
>     - Separate legal identity → business continues if an owner leaves or dies
>     - Can sell shares to family and friends → raise larger amounts of capital to fund the theatre
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Accounts are public → competing theatres can see ET’s financial results
>     - Shares are hard to transfer in a private company → may slow down future fundraising
>     - More legal paperwork to set up and run → audits and filings increase time and cost
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - A partnership offers full control, simple set-up and keeps profits private, but brings unlimited liability and limited funds
>   - Forming a private limited company protects personal assets and allows bigger capital injections, but adds legal formalities, the need to make accounts public and less flexibility

**Playsafe Playground Equipment (PPE)**

Kaari has always been creative and made wooden toys for her two children when they were young. Her children are now at school, so Kaari decided to start her own business making wooden playground equipment.

Kaari started PPE as a sole trader business three years ago in country Z. She wants an income from the business but also wants to spend time with her children. Kaari wants the business to remain small. However, if the business grows Kaari may need to change to another type of business organisation. Kaari carries out all the management roles in the business.

Kaari uses job production to produce high quality, individually designed playground equipment. Kaari designs all the equipment herself and she employs 3 skilled workers to help her make the products. PPE currently makes both large and small items of playground equipment each week.

Kaari uses cost-plus pricing as every item of playground equipment uses different quantities of raw materials. She sells small items of playground equipment to retailers and large items of playground equipment to the Government. There are many competitors in this market.

Kaari plans to obtain new machinery which will cost \$20 000. She is considering using crowd-funding as this is one way to raise capital for new business investment. Other options include leasing the machinery or asking the bank for a loan.

Kaari has developed a new unique product this year. There are no other similar products in the market.

{align=center} **Appendix 1**

{align=center} **Advertisement for PPE**

Buy your playground equipment from us.

At PPE we manufacture high quality playground equipment and have better designs than our competitors.

All our equipment has been fully tested and is guaranteed to meet legal safety standards. We are the main supplier of playground equipment to the Government for public parks - so you know our equipment can be trusted!

Contact us today for a price list.

{align=center} **Appendix 2**

{align=center} **Cost and revenue information for PPE in 2021**

|   | **Small item of playground****equipment** | **Large item of playground****equipment** |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Average selling price | \$100 | \$1 000 |
| Average cost of manufacture | \$25 | \$500 |
| Output each week | 15 | 3 |

{align=center} **Appendix 3**

{align=center} **Newspaper article – Main News 1st October 2021**

{align=center} **Children need to get more exercise and play outside**

Research suggests that playing outside helps children relax after school and improves their health.

The Government in country Z has allocated \$10m to spend on improving children’s playgrounds in public places. This means there will be \$5 000 to spend on equipment for each public playground.

Retailers have reported increasing demand for small items of playground equipment as parents want to have these products at home. This trend is expected to continue.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of **two **suitable types of business organisation for PPE. Which do you think is the best one if PPE grows? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/jun-2021-paper-2-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
PPE currently operates as a sole trader business, but as it grows, Kaari may consider changing to a partnership. This would allow Kaari to bring in one or more partners to help manage and finance the growing business **[An]**. It could provide additional capital to purchase the \$20,000 machinery **[Ap]** PPE needs. Partners could also bring valuable skills and share responsibilities, which would help Kaari maintain work-life balance **[An]** as she wants to spend time with her children **[Ap]**. However, partnerships have unlimited liability, meaning Kaari would continue to be partly responsible for any debts **[An]**. There's also potential for disputes between partners, which could slow down decision-making **[An]**

Alternatively, forming a private limited company would give PPE's owners, including Kaari, the protection of limited liability. This means her personal assets would be protected if the business struggled with debts **[An], **protecting her young family **[Ap]**. A private limited company structure could also make it easier to raise capital by selling shares **[An]**. However, there are more complex legal requirements and regulations to follow compared to a sole trader, which, as a sole trader, Kaari has not had to deal with **[Ap]**, and she is likely to have to pay for legal advice, increasing costs **[An]**

Overall, a private limited company seems the best option if PPE grows substantially **[E]**. Although it will be more complex to run, the limited liability protection is valuable as the business takes on more financial commitments, like the new machinery **[Ap]**, because PPE's owners' assets would be protected **[An]**. This would not be the case if it became a partnership **[E]**. It also provides a professional image **[E]**, which may help PPE win more government contracts for playground equipment **[Ap]**

>

>   - A private limited company offers limited liability and fresh capital, but legal formalities and reduced privacy may not suit a small, custobuiltld business

{align=center} **Gemma’s Jewels (GJ)**

Gemma set up GJ as a sole trader 5 years ago in country Z. She started by selling rings and bracelets from a rented shop. She used her own savings to start the business. The first year was successful. After this first year Gemma decided to expand by selling more expensive items of jewellery. Gemma thinks it is important to set clear business objectives. She wants her business to increase sales by 10% each year and to increase market share.

As the business grew Gemma needed more finance for a computer, inventory and working capital to avoid liquidity problems. She decided to convert the business to a private limited company and sell shares to members of her family. Gemma still owns more than 50% of the shares in GJ.

In 2019, Gemma purchased a franchise from Beautywise Jewellery. This means GJ is now only able to sell Beautywise products in its shop. GJ has to purchase all of its inventory from Beautywise and in addition pay 20% of gross profit to Beautywise. More details about the franchise are in the advertisement in Appendix 1.

Gemma has developed a website so customers can order online. Customers can also download a mobile (cell) phone app to view and order jewellery.

Gemma plans to open a second shop as a Beautywise franchise in a nearby town. She has to decide which method of sales promotion to use. GJ needs to recruit a manager for the new shop. The manager will be responsible for operating the shop and making most of the decisions about which items of inventory to buy. The manager will also need to ensure excellent customer service is provided and that the new employees are motivated and working efficiently.

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Advertisement for Beautywise Jewellery Franchise**

**Become a franchisee to sell Beautywise Jewellery and improve your chances of success!!**

What we offer you:

- Be the only shop in your area that sells Beautywise jewellery
- Beautywise will advertise nationally on television and in newspapers
- Help and advice on decoration of the shop and training for employees and the franchisee
- Ethically sourced jewellery imported especially for Beautywise
- The franchise fee is just \$50 000 per year!

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Newspaper article- Daily News **

**External factors affecting the jewellery market in country Z**

The demand for jewellery in country Z is likely to be affected by some recent changes. Consumers are becoming more aware of the ethical issues involved in jewellery production in some countries. The exchange rate of the currency of country Z is likely to depreciate over the next 12 months. The Government is planning changes to tax rates which might reduce the effects of the current economic boom.

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Information on three possible locations for the new shop**

| **Annual costs** | **Town A** | **Town B** | **Town C** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shop rent | \$45 000 per year for 5 years | \$35 000 per year for 10 years | \$20 000 per year for 15 years |
| Wages and salaries | \$80 000 | \$70 000 | \$60 000 |
| Heating and lighting | \$5 000 | \$5 000 | \$3 000 |
| Estimated gross profit | \$400 000 | \$300 000 | \$200 000 |

Note: Franchise fee is \$50 000 per year and 20% of gross profit is paid to Beautywise.

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of buying the Beautywise franchise. Do you think Gemma was right to buy the franchise? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-2-case-study---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
One key advantage is that Beautywise is a known jewellery brand, which reduces the chances of business failure for Gemma's Jewels. Beautywise will advertise nationally on television and in newspapers **[Ap]**, which lowers Gemma's marketing costs** [An]**. Additionally, Beautywise provides help and advice on decoration of the shop and training for employees and the franchisee **[Ap]**, saving Gemma time and money on staff development **[An]**

However, there are significant disadvantages. The franchise has a high cost of \$50,000 per year, plus 20% of gross profit **[Ap]** paid to Beautywise. This means less profit as a reward for Gemma **[An]**. The case study also states that GJ is now only able to sell Beautywise products in its shop **[Ap]**, which restricts the variety of jewellery available, which may be less appealing to customers **[An]**

On balance, I think Gemma was right to buy the franchise. As a relatively new business of 5 years **[Ap]**, buying a franchise will likely make it easier for GJ to obtain finance from banks for expansion  **[E]**. Gemma's plans to open a second shop  **[Ap]**, and banks are often more willing to lend to franchises due to their lower risk of failure **[E]**. Although Gemma loses some independence in decision-making, the support and established brand of Beautywise could help GJ achieve its objective of increasing sales by 10% each year **[Ap]**. The franchise's ethical sourcing of jewellery also aligns with the growing consumer awareness of ethical issues **[Ap] **mentioned in the newspaper article, potentially attracting more customers **[E]**

>

{align=center} **Cell Covers (CC) **

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes. 

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows. 

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading. 

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present. 

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Newspaper article in Main News **

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!! 

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

| Revenue | 800 000 |
| --- | ---: |
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |
| of which: Inventory | 5 000 |
| Current liabilities | 15 000 |

Explain **two **possible reasons why Aisha set up CC as a business partnership.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:

One advantage of becoming a private limited company is limited liability for LMA's owners **[K]**. However, there are more legal formalities **[K]**. As a private limited company, LMA would need to publish its accounts and hold annual general meetings. >   - Give two valid advantages to increase added value to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - For each advantage, refer to the business case study to achieve both application [Ap] marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - Access to more capital (than unlimited company) / can raise capital by selling shares [k] to start making cars [ap]
>   - Control over who buys shares/less risk of takeover (than public limited company) [k] which may be important as there is a lot of competition [ap]
>   - Continuity of existence [k]
>   - Separate legal identity [k]
>   - (Its shareholders benefit from) limited liability / incorporated [k]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited.

parts.problem_md: **Define **‘unincorporated business’.
parts.solution_md:
An unincorporated business is often a small firm **[K]** that does not have a separate legal identity to its owners **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**

> **[mark-scheme]**

>

>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - A business that does not have a separate legal identity [2]
> 
> OR
>

parts.problem_md:
**Outline**, with reference to TYA, the difference between a limited company and an unincorporated business.

> **[case-study]**
> TYA is a limited company which manufactures 300 000 cars a year. It has 600 employees. TYA has high fixed costs. The Managing Director wants to improve efficiency in the factory. He said: ‘Globalisation is changing how businesses operate. Many manufacturing businesses are considering whether to relocate their operations to other countries.’
parts.solution_md:
A limited company has a separate legal identity **[K]** to its owners, so assets such as the car factory **[Ap]** and the 300,000 cars **[Ap]** are owned by the business rather than the individual shareholders. In contrast, the owners and the business are the same for an unincorporated business **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Unincorporated businesses include sole traders and partnerships, so consider features of these in your comparison

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2; Application 2
> 
>   - Give two valid points, one for each of the ownership types, to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - For each point, refer to the business case study to achieve both application [Ap] marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Points might include:
> 
>   - A limited company has separate legal identity [k] so assets such as the factory [ap] and the 600 cars [ap] are owned by the business rather than the individual, whereas the owners and the business are the same for an unincorporated business [k]
>   - An unincorporated business has unlimited liability [k] whereas the risk for shareholders/owners of a limited company is limited to the amount invested [k] in the car business [ap] so they may be less concerned about the high fixed costs [ap]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

parts.problem_md:
**Outline **how having limited liability might benefit DNG’s shareholders.

> **[case-study]**
> DNG provides electricity to 16 million customers. It is a limited company which means DNG’s shareholders benefit from limited liability. DNG is planning to stop using coal to produce its electricity. Pressure groups had an influence on this decision. The Managing Director knows there will be an opportunity cost to making this change. She is considering the best way to communicate this important information to DNG’s 6500 employees.
parts.solution_md:
Shareholders' risk is limited **[K]** to the amount they have invested in the electrical business **[Ap]**, which means that their personal assets are protected **[K]** if the business decision to stop the use of coal **[Ap] **fails

> **[exam-tip]**
> Your answer must refer to the business owners (shareholders) rather than to the business itself

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2; Application 2
> 
>   - Give two valid benefits to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - For each benefit, refer to the business case study to achieve both application [Ap] marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Benefits may include:
> 
>   - Shareholders risk is limited to the amount invested [k] in this electricity business [ap]
>   - Protects personal assets [k] in case the business decision to contribute to sustainable development does not work [ap]
>   - Encourages (potential/existing) shareholders to invest [k] in the electricity generation business [ap]
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

parts.problem_md: **Define **‘public limited company’.
parts.solution_md:
A public limited company is a business owned by shareholders, **[K] **that can sell shares to the public on the stock exchange **[K]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't confuse public limited companies, which are a form of business ownership, with the public sector, which is a part of the economy

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Give a clearly-stated, valid definition to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Businesses owned by shareholders, but they can sell shares to the public and their shares are tradeable on the stock exchange [2]
> 
> OR
> 
> - Often a large company, owned by shareholders who have limited liability. The company can sell its shares to the general public [2]
> 
> OR
> 
> - A company that sells its shares to the general public through a stock exchange (because the company can sell shares to anyone, it can raise massive amounts of money) [2]
> 
> OR
> 
> - A business whose shares can be freely bought and sold to the general public [2]
> 
> OR
> 
> - Partial definition e.g. a business that can sell shares [1]
